title: Canonical device security model
description: Vendor-neutral security model produced by the mapping engine for one device. Every leaf is a {value, state, evidence} triple. Every collection carries its own state so an unparsed list is never mistaken for an empty one. Field list source: packs/CLAUDE.md v1. Rename nothing; add freely. The x-absent annotation is the recommended absent-semantics for packs that map the field; a vendor pack may override it per mapping.

hostname.description: The name the device calls itself, shown in its prompt and used to identify it in reports.

vendor.description: Which vendor pack recognised this configuration, for example Cisco IOS or Juniper Junos.

os_family.description: The operating system family running on the device, such as IOS, NX-OS, Junos or FortiOS.

os_version.description: The software or firmware release the configuration was written for.

model.description: The hardware platform or chassis model of the device.

serial.description: The hardware serial number or processor board identifier of the device.

enabled.description: Whether the device accepts encrypted remote command-line logins over Secure Shell.

version.description: Which SSH protocol version the server allows; version 1 is broken and only version 2 should be accepted.

timeout.description: How many seconds an SSH client has to finish logging in before the server drops the connection.

max_auth_tries.description: How many wrong passwords an SSH client may try in one connection before it is disconnected.

enabled.description: Whether the device accepts unencrypted cleartext remote logins over Telnet.
Whether the built-in web management interface is reachable over plain unencrypted HTTP.
Whether the built-in web management interface is reachable over encrypted HTTPS.
Whether centralised authentication, authorisation and accounting (AAA, for example RADIUS or TACACS+) is turned on.

algorithm.description: The hashing algorithm protecting the privileged-mode password, kept after redaction so weak hashes can be detected (for example type 5 MD5 versus type 9 scrypt).

password_min_length.description: The shortest password the device will accept when a local password is set.

present.description: Whether a legal warning message is shown to anyone before they log in.

local_users.description: Accounts defined directly on the device rather than in a central directory.

name.description: The login name of a locally defined user account.

privilege.description: How much the local account is allowed to do once logged in; higher means more administrative power.

password_algorithm.description: The hashing or encryption scheme used to store this local account's password.

idle_timeout.description: How many seconds an inactive management session stays open before the device logs it out.

enabled.description: Whether the device records system and security event messages at all.

level.description: The minimum severity of event that gets recorded, such as informational, warnings or errors.

buffered_enabled.description: Whether event messages are kept in a local memory buffer on the device.

servers.description: Remote syslog servers that event messages are sent to for central storage.

authenticate.description: Whether time updates must be cryptographically authenticated before the clock accepts them.

servers.description: Time servers the device synchronises its clock against.

version.description: Which SNMP monitoring protocol version is in use; v1 and v2c send passwords in cleartext, v3 can encrypt.

traps_enabled.description: Whether the device pushes unsolicited alert notifications to a monitoring station.

communities.description: Shared community strings that act as passwords for SNMP v1/v2c monitoring access.

string_redacted.description: The community string with its secret removed at ingest, kept only so entries can be told apart.

access.description: Whether this community can only read monitoring data or can also change configuration.

interfaces.description: Physical and logical network ports on the device, each with its own security settings.

name.description: The identifier of the port, such as GigabitEthernet0/1, taken from the enclosing configuration block.

shutdown.description: Whether the port has been administratively disabled so it passes no traffic.

description.description: Free-text label an administrator wrote on the port to say what it connects to.

proxy_arp.description: Whether the port answers address-resolution requests on behalf of other hosts, which can let traffic bypass intended routing.

ip_redirects.description: Whether the port sends ICMP redirect messages telling hosts to use a different gateway.

unreachables.description: Whether the port replies with ICMP destination-unreachable messages, which can help attackers map the network.

switchport_mode.description: Whether a switch port carries a single VLAN (access) or many VLANs (trunk), or negotiates it dynamically.

access_vlan.description: The VLAN number an access-mode switch port places its traffic in.

vty_lines.description: Virtual terminal lines that accept remote management logins.

transport_input.description: Which remote login protocols this terminal line accepts, for example SSH only, Telnet, or all.

access_class.description: The access list restricting which source addresses may log in on this terminal line.

exec_timeout.description: How many seconds an idle remote login on this line stays open before it is disconnected.

lists.description: Access control lists: named or numbered filters that permit or deny traffic.

name.description: The name or number identifying an access control list.

entries.description: The ordered filter statements inside one access control list.

seq.description: The position of a filter statement within its access list; lower numbers are checked first.

action.description: Whether matching traffic is allowed through (permit) or dropped (deny).

cdp_enabled.description: Whether the device advertises its identity and software version to neighbours using Cisco Discovery Protocol.

lldp_enabled.description: Whether the device advertises its identity to neighbours using the vendor-neutral Link Layer Discovery Protocol.

line.description: 1-based source line. Null only when state is defaulted (no line exists).

collection.description: A list plus its own provenance. state=unknown means the list was not parsed, and items MUST be empty; the evaluator returns NOT_DETERMINED for any quantifier over it instead of a vacuous PASS.
